about: the path claims of Knowledge in mmhc and rsmax2 (default phases), rerun after their restrict phase reads the knowledge: on simulated data, each method with true claims against the same fit without them, and against bnlearn given the same knowledge, with the default score and with ebic_gamma=0 (mmhc_bic, rsmax2_bic), the plain BIC of bnlearn's bic-g. These rows replace those of mmhc and rsmax2 in published/0.17.0/knowledge-paths.json.
build: Andrey pre-release build of 26 November 2026 on the 0.20.0 release branch (commit 117e0fd31, version string 0.19.0); the lane with the mmhc_bic and rsmax2_bic variants added

lanes.cpdag: mmhc, rsmax2, mmhc_bic, rsmax2_bic: linear-Gaussian, Erdos-Renyi, standardized; d 10, 20, 50; n 500, 2000; expected degree 2 and 4; claims on 5, 10, 30% of the ordered pairs

verdict_rule: per method, cell, part, and fraction: D = errors(with true claims) - errors(without) per dataset, seeds 0-19; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies above 0, better when below; a worse row counts only when the same row on seeds 100-119 is worse too in the same measure. The cpdag lane judges two measures, errors and dag_errors (dag_* fields), and a row worse again in either counts. Floor: the interval of errors - empty-graph errors must lie below 0. A part of a method passes when no judged row is worse again, every judged row is below the floor, and every dataset was fit.
error_metric: cpdag: errors is the structural Hamming distance (andrey.metrics.shd) to the class the truth and the fit's true claims define, the true CPDAG without claims and the MPDAG of the true class under the claims with them; dag_errors is the endpoint-aware distance to the true DAG (an edge directed as the DAG directs it 0, an undirected edge 1, a reversed, missing, or extra edge 2); reversed_with and reversed_without are the mean numbers of edges directed against the true DAG; edges_directed_by_claims counts, on pairs adjacent in the truth, the edges directed with the claims beyond those directed without, and of_them_against_the_true_dag those directed against the true DAG
dropped_note: claims is the number of true claims given to the fits of a row and dropped the number the fits dropped as unmet by the graph they found; knowledge_error counts fits that raised
false_claims_note: rows with arm false state 10% of the ordered pairs wrongly: context, not judged

references.about: each method against bnlearn given the same knowledge, on the datasets of the lane above; seeds 0-19, worse rows of the like-for-like comparison repeated on seeds 100-119

packages.bnlearn.mmhc: bnlearn 5.2.1 mmhc, Fisher z (zf) at alpha 0.05 and score bic-g, whitelist and blacklist
packages.bnlearn.rsmax2: bnlearn 5.2.1 rsmax2 with restrict mmpc and maximize hc, Fisher z at alpha 0.05 and score bic-g, whitelist and blacklist

references.translation: bnlearn takes edges, not paths: a forbidden path a -> b becomes the forbidden edge a -> b; a required path on a pair adjacent in the true graph becomes the required edge a -> b; a required path on any other pair has no edge form and is left out. A required edge says more than the path it comes from: it states that the pair is adjacent.
references.arms: same_edges: the method with the translated edges as required and forbidden against bnlearn with the same edges. claims_against_reference: the method with the path claims against bnlearn with the translated edges; not like for like, reported on seeds 0-19, and repeated on fresh seeds only where a cell was rerun for another row. without_knowledge: both without knowledge. mmhc_bic and rsmax2_bic are mmhc and rsmax2 with ebic_gamma=0, the plain BIC of bnlearn's bic-g.
references.rule: per method, reference, cell, part, and fraction: D = errors(method) - errors(reference) per dataset both fit, dag_errors; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D (10,000 resamples) lies above 0; a worse row counts when the same row on seeds 100-119 is worse too. A part of a method meets the bar when it passes the checks above and, with the same knowledge as the reference (same_edges), no judged row of its own, or of the all-parts runs for required_paths, is worse again against bnlearn, with the default score and with ebic_gamma=0; with the default score every judged row must also be below the floor. The floor of the ebic_gamma=0 arms is reported under plain_bic_floor, not judged. In status, bar_met says whether the part met the bar and reasons lists the checks it did not pass; supported is the part's status, and a part that is supported without meeting the bar says in gap what it differs in.

reasons: with ebic_gamma=0, same_edges against bnlearn.mmhc (required_paths): 4 of 36 rows worse again
with ebic_gamma=0, same_edges against bnlearn.mmhc (all parts): 4 of 36 rows worse again
required_paths.gap: With ebic_gamma=0 and most true edges given as required, the fit keeps a few more false edges than bnlearn's fit given the same edges, in the rows worse_again_rows lists for the ebic_gamma=0 arm under references.against; with the default score no row is worse again. The difference lies in the candidate search. Andrey tests each candidate against every subset of the current members, as the MMPC paper defines. bnlearn's forward phase starts each target's candidate set from its whitelisted neighbors and tests only the sets that hold the last of them.
